paragraphs: Mentioned in Eruvin, chapter 6, halakhah 10. Hyman identifies him as R' Yehudah Nesiah.[^1][^2]

notes.text: פ״ו ה״י explicitly gives chapter 6, halakhah 10. That form suggests the Jerusalem Talmud, but the corpus is not explicit and no named edition is independently checked.
נסייא and נשיאה are preserved as Nesia and Nesiah. Their identification is Hyman’s statement, not an authority merge. Both personal title abbreviations remain R'.
